the effect that mean reversion has on the optimal limit order prices.
the effect of mean reversion on limit order trading and the optimal limit order prices.

when the underlying price has a mean reversion property, then for times far from the terminal the optimal limit order prices are constant and do not track the underlying asset price.
when the market is sufficiently liquid, then limit order prices track the price, while when it is illiquid, they do not.

limit order prices are not always influenced by the underlying price and that the duration of this influence is determined by the liquidity of the model.
limit order prices do not track the underlying mean reverting price, and that the time horizon for this behavior depends on the liquidity in the market.
